facts.big: Could we have the check? · Let us split it
facts.label: Pedir e dividir a conta
facts.sub: Peça com Could we have the check, please? Sugira com Let us split it in two. Pergunte How much is the total? e diga We each pay twenty. Peça Two separate checks, please.

facts.label: A conta
facts.sub: Nos EUA, a conta se chama check ou bill. O garçom só traz quando você pede, e é normal esperar sem pressa. Peça com “Could we have the check, please?”

facts.label: Dividir
facts.sub: Amigos costumam dividir a conta igualmente ou cada um paga o que comeu. Para isso, peça contas separadas antes de pedir, ou diga “Let us split it.”

compare.br: In Brazil, people often ask “a conta” and divide it by pessoa, and the waiter brings a machine for cards.
compare.tip: Say: “Could we have the check, please?”
compare.us: In the USA, people ask for “the check”, and servers can bring separate checks.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: You ask for “the check” at the end of a meal.
You must wait until the waiter leaves.
items.why: You can ask when you are ready.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

pages.title: Two halves · 1/3
paragraphs: It is nine o’clock on a Friday night in Seattle. Two friends finish dinner in a cozy restaurant. The plates are empty, and the lights are low. Mina and Hal talk about their week. The waiter walks by with a tray of drinks. It is time to pay.
“That was a great dinner.” says Hal. “Yes! Excuse me, could we have the check, please?” says Mina. “Let us split it in two.” says Hal.

pages.title: Two halves · 3/3
paragraphs: “Okay. Could we have two separate checks next time, because it is easier?” says Mina. “Sure. Good idea!” says Hal. The waiter brings the check in a small folder. Hal puts his card inside.
